title: I Enforced the Community-Apiary Smoker Log on the Chair Whose Nephew Skipped It

parts.text: I arrived at hive row B at 8:05 a.m. and chair Tamsin's nephew was already pumping our numbered smoker. The board said: ONE SMOKER. SIGN THE LOG. FUEL STAYS WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was thirty-eight, hive steward, holding a veil that listed our yard. Tamsin shrugged. "Family is the yard." I photographed the board, the log, and his bellows on our stand. Then I asked for the fuel sheet. At 8:13 the apiary pinged why the nephew's name was not on our smoker. I kept my voice bee-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A paper log is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The apiary can see the nephew's bellows on our stand during our checkout.

social.video_title: He pumped our numbered smoker without the log — Part 1/2
social.description: Apiary row, a nephew on our stand, a smoker log Tamsin posted. I logged the bellows. Would you have asked for the fuel sheet?

parts.text: Tamsin called it a calm until the steward asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the stand still. The smoker went back to our hook. Tamsin ran her own checkout and told the next chair atmosphere was always about the bees. Bees is a word chairs use when a log exists. Yard policy now has a second line: FAMILY IS NOT THE YARD. I keep our fuel on a labeled tin. Tamsin brown-bags her jokes. The row finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
